# connect — agent bootstrap (llms.txt)

> `connect` is the client CLI for the ab0t **integration mesh**: connect
> third-party services once, then call their APIs through one authenticated
> proxy, run normalized tools, and route/observe webhooks — all headless after
> the one-time consent. This file is the **bootstrap entrypoint for an AI
> agent**: follow it top to bottom to install the tool, load its operating
> knowledge, and start acting through connections. Everything linked below is
> in this repo.

## What this is

The mesh (`https://connect.service.ab0t.com`) is a multi-tenant gateway
with three surfaces:

- **Proxy** — transparent passthrough to a connected provider's own API; the
 mesh injects the credential, refreshes OAuth tokens, rate-limits, audits.
- **Tools (UTS)** — each provider's operations as normalized, input-validated
 `category/tool/execute` tools. Prefer these for agents.
- **Webhooks** — inbound provider events matched to your subscriptions and
 delivered to your URL, HMAC-signed and retried.

A **connection** is a stored, encrypted credential for one account of one
service. Creating it = consent ONCE; acting through its `connection_id` is
unlimited and headless.

## Bootstrap sequence

1. **Install the binary.**
 ```sh
 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ab0t-com/connect-cli/main/install.sh | sh
 ```
 (Multi-platform, checksum-verified, atomic, idempotent.) Or run the matching
 binary from [`release/`](release/) directly — static builds, no deps.

2. **Authenticate.** Headless is the agent path:
 ```sh
 export CONNECT_API_KEY=ab0t_sk_live_.. # a service/user key from the auth mesh
 connect status
 ```
 Humans can use `connect login` (browser). API key auth needs no browser.

3. **Load your operating instructions (system prompt).** Read and adopt
 [`prompts/AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`](prompts/AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md) as your
 system prompt for driving connect.

4. **Load the driving skill.** Read
 [`skills/connect/SKILL.md`](skills/connect/SKILL.md) and its references — it
 encodes the connection model, the proxy-vs-tools decision, the headless/
 agentic connect loop, and webhook verification. For the raw REST API without
 the CLI, the live OpenAPI is published at
 `https://connect.service.ab0t.com/openapi.json`.

5. **Discover and connect.**
 ```sh
 connect services list # the connectable catalog
 connect connections list # what you already have (connection_id)
 connect add sendgrid --api-key SG.xxxx # API-key services connect headlessly
 connect add github # OAuth services need one-time human consent
 ```
 OAuth requires a browser once. For fully agentic OAuth (service accounts,
 device-code, pre-provisioning) read
 [`skills/connect/references/agentic-connections.md`](skills/connect/references/agentic-connections.md).

6. **Act through a connection.**
 ```sh
 connect call <connection_id> GET /user/repos # raw proxy passthrough
 connect tools catalog # discover tools
 connect tools show google-calendar/create_event --examples # one tool's schema + examples
 # execute via the API: POST /uts/v1/tools/{category}/{tool}/execute
 ```

7. **Receive events.**
 ```sh
 connect subscribe github push --connection <conn> --url https://myapp.com/hook
 connect webhooks deliveries list # observe / debug deliveries
 ```

## Map

- [README.md](README.md) — overview, install, the three surfaces, consent-vs-action.
- [install.sh](install.sh) — POSIX, HTTPS-only, sha256-verified, multi-platform installer.
- [release/](release/) — per-platform binaries, `checksums.txt`, `VERSION`.
- [docs/USAGE.md](docs/USAGE.md) — every command; the connection model; proxy/tools/webhooks; headless auth.
- [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md) — the connectable provider catalog (incl. Xero / Meta Ads / Google Ads).
- [prompts/AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md](prompts/AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md) — system prompt for driving connect with an LLM.
- [skills/](skills/) — 11 agent skills (Agent Skills standard). Read `connect-concepts` first.
 Understand: `connect-concepts/` (mental model + glossary), `connect-security/` (encryption, consent, signature verify, tenant isolation).
 Surfaces: `connect/` (the daily-driver CLI), `connect-connections/` (connection model + setup, OAuth vs API-key, multi-tenant, connection_id), `connect-proxy/` (the `/proxy/{connection_id}` passthrough), `connect-tools/` (validated UTS tools — discover/validate/execute/batch), `connect-realtime/` (receive events: webhooks HTTP-push + websockets `wss ?token=` stream), `connect-auth/` (CLI auth & profiles, headless).
 Build/operate: `connect-recipes/` (end-to-end cookbook incl. multi-tenant SaaS + agents), `connect-troubleshooting/` (unified error reference + rate limits + debug), `connect-rest-api/` (call the public REST API directly, no CLI).

## Key facts an agent should internalize

- **Act through a `connection_id`.** Everything you DO (proxy, tools, webhooks)
 is scoped to one connection. List yours with `connect connections list`.
- **Consent once, act forever.** Creating a connection is the only step that may
 need a browser (OAuth). After that it's headless. You cannot inject OAuth
 tokens via the API-key path — that's by design.
- **Prefer tools over raw proxy** when a tool exists: input validation,
 structured errors, ownership checks. Fall back to `call`/`proxy` for
 operations not yet covered by a tool.
- **Tenancy is enforced server-side.** Wrong-type connection → `400`; missing →
 `404`; another tenant's connection → `403`. You only ever touch your own org.
- **Webhook signatures:** `X-Webhook-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256(raw body,
 signing_secret)>`. `v1` is HMAC of the **raw body only** (not Stripe-style —
 `t` is not part of the signed payload). Verify before trusting a delivery.
- **The `*.service.ab0t.com` hosts are the product's public endpoints** —
 expected, not secrets. `connect.service.ab0t.com` is the API base.
- **`-o json`** on any command for machine-readable output; agents get a
 structured `_next` field (`next_command`, `why`, `alternatives`) to drive the
 next step.
